1.explanation:
We reproduce the negative-time marks by injecting a performance.mark() before the page’s NavigationStart event.  
Puppeteer’s page.evaluateOnNewDocument runs that script in the page context at document start (i.e. before navigation timing begins), so when the mark is recorded it has a timestamp less than zero relative to NavigationStart.  
After navigation completes, we add further marks and measures and then dump performance.getEntries().  Marks injected pre-NavigationStart will appear with negative startTime, matching the bug scenario.
1.bug_scenario:
When running Lighthouse (or the DevTools “User Timings” extension) on https://www.chromestatus.com/features there are Performance → User Timing entries with negative start times:

• Mark: -184.69ms – mark_features_unveil_start
• Mark: -184.53ms – mark_features_loaded_start
…

These negative values occur because the first marks are recorded before the NavigationStart event (i.e. before the trace’s zero-point), causing the audit/formatter to display negative offsets.
